short: The brutal final defeat of the Jacobite army that permanently ended the Stuart cause.
full:
On 16 April 1746, the exhausted and hungry Jacobite army faced a larger, well-supplied government force commanded by the Duke of Cumberland on the bleak moorland of Culloden. The flat, boggy terrain negated the devastating impact of the traditional Highland charge, allowing government artillery and disciplined musket fire to tear through the advancing Jacobite ranks.

The battle was brief and bloody, ending in a catastrophic rout for Charles Edward Stuart's forces. In the aftermath, Cumberland's troops systematically hunted down fleeing survivors and initiated a brutal pacification of the Highlands. Culloden was the last pitched battle fought on British soil and marked the absolute destruction of the Jacobite movement.
